Hero.Title: Learn Physical AI – vendor-neutral, hands-on
Hero.Lead: How do cognitive robots learn, how do you test them, and how do you introduce them safely in your own operations? EmAI Academy teaches this to decision makers and engineers: with open models, real hardware and no vendor lock-in.
Hero.DiagramLabel: Curriculum diagram: nine skills connected by their prerequisites. The Decider path runs through skills 1, 8 and 9. The Builder path runs through 1, then 2 or 3, then 4, 5 or 6, and ends at 7.
Hero.Legend: Each node is a skill. Lines show what builds on what.

Tested.Title: Tested ourselves
Tested.Body: Everything we teach, we have tried on our own robots – including the places where it does not work.

Neutral.Title: Vendor-neutral
Neutral.Body: We do not sell robots. You learn criteria to evaluate any platform yourself.

Open.Title: Openly shared
Open.Body: Open models, open datasets, open tools such as LeRobot. What you learn here is yours.

Tracks.Title: Two learning paths, one shared foundation
Tracks.Intro: Both paths start with skill 1. Then you decide whether you want to evaluate and introduce Physical AI, or train robots yourself.

Decider.Name: Decider
Decider.Who: For executives, innovation, production and IT leads.
Decider.Body: You understand what cognitive robots can do today, where the risks are, and how to plan data sovereignty and security from day one.
Decider.Outcome: compare vendors neutrally, assess risks and set up a pilot with a clear business case.

Builder.Name: Builder
Builder.Body: You collect data via teleoperation, train imitation learning and VLA policies, use simulation and deploy models to the robot measurably.
Builder.Outcome: take a policy from data collection to an evaluated deployment on your own.

Curriculum.Title: The curriculum
Curriculum.Intro: Nine skills, each with clear prerequisites. The skill tree always shows what you already know and what unlocks next.

S1.Name: Physical AI fundamentals
S1.Body: What sets cognitive robots apart from classic automation: perception, foundation models, embodiment.

S2.Name: Robot hardware & embodiments
S2.Body: Actuators, sensors, hands and grippers. Why a robot's form decides what it can learn.

S3.Name: Robotics software fundamentals
S3.Body: ROS 2, coordinate frames, kinematics and control – the toolkit underneath every policy.

S4.Name: Data for robot learning
S4.Body: Teleoperation, data formats, quality and data sovereignty. Good demonstrations are half the policy.

S5.Name: Imitation learning & VLAs
S5.Body: From ACT to vision-language-action models: train and fine-tune policies from demonstrations.

S6.Name: Simulation & reinforcement learning
S6.Body: Sim-to-real, domain randomization and RL for locomotion and manipulation.

S7.Name: Evaluation & deployment
S7.Body: Measure reproducibly, find failures systematically and bring models to the robot under control.

S8.Name: Safety, security & sovereignty
S8.Body: Machine safety, the AI Act, attack surfaces and data flows – and how you stay in control.

S9.Name: Introducing Physical AI in your company
S9.Body: Prioritise use cases, plan pilots, bring people along and secure operations.

Lab.Title: Learning happens on real hardware
Lab.Intro: The practical skills lead to two platforms we operate ourselves. Both are controlled openly, without a vendor cloud.

G1.Name: Unitree G1 EDU with Dex3 hands
G1.Body: Whole-body platform for teleoperation, data collection and manipulation with two force-controlled three-finger hands.
G1.SensorsValue: Livox Mid-360 LiDAR, RealSense D435i, IMU

SO101.Name: SO-101 robot arm with LeRobot
SO101.Body: An affordable entry into robot learning: record demonstrations with the leader arm, train a policy, run it on the follower arm.

Cta.Title: Start with skill 1
Cta.Body: The fundamentals are the same for both paths and free. Then choose your way in the skill tree.
